A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NEDS research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural encoding and decoding experiments, brain-region classification, masking and embedding ablations, and monkey-reaching results in Appendix H.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their results, including the appendix ablations and monkey-reaching evaluation.

M1.justification: The masking schemes, transformer architecture, session adaptation, losses, and inference tasks remain unchanged. Section 3.4 newly specifies replacement with a learned mask token, but does not establish a revision to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate IBL mouse decision-making data and MC-RTT monkey-reaching data. Neural encoding, behavioral decoding, and five-region neuron classification retain the same coverage; Appendix H was already present in v1.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain linear regression, reduced-rank regression, unimodal NEDS, POYO+, and NDT2. Appendix H retains the MLP and unimodal NEDS comparators. The added citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The animal and trial splits, preprocessing, metrics, tuning budgets, model configurations, five-fold brain-region evaluation, and Appendix H procedures are unchanged. Newly stated baseline temporal inputs and parameter counts document existing experiments without establishing changed settings.

E4.justification: The masking, model-size, and embedding ablations in Appendices B, D, and G remain unchanged, as do the qualitative predictions and brain-region embedding analyses. Appendix G loses a qualification, but no analysis or result is removed.

E5.justification: Reporting practices remain unchanged: Tables 1 and 10 report means and standard errors across animals or sessions, and Table 11 reports means and standard deviations across ten sessions. No repeated-run count, seed specification, or uncertainty-estimation procedure changes.

E6.justification: The result figures, tables, and reported findings retain the same values and rankings. Examples include NEDS encoding of 0.27 ± 0.03 bps in Table 10, 83% brain-region classification accuracy, and MC-RTT velocity decoding R2 of 0.72 in Table 12.

T1.justification: The conditional-expectation definitions in Section 3.2, generative formulation in Equation 1, distributional assumptions, and bits-per-spike definition in Appendix A are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and discussion retain the same claims: unified encoding and decoding, state-of-the-art performance, benefits from scaling, and emergent brain-region information in neuron embeddings.

C2.justification: Appendix G removes the specific qualification that single-session embedding ablations are more sensitive to hyperparameters and random seeds, along with its unresolved appendix reference. The main limitations and interpretations of experimental results remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds a project/code link, specifies learned mask-token replacement in Section 3.4, and explains the linear baselines' use of all timesteps in Section 4.2. Figure 2 newly reports parameter-count ranges for linear and reduced-rank models; detailed appendix configurations and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Wang et al. (2025) to the discussion of large-scale encoding and Lurz et al. (2020) to multi-animal modeling. The research positioning remains stable. Schulz et al. changes from its 2024 preprint citation to its 2025 publication, representing the same work.

P1.justification: Most prose and the scientific section sequence remain unchanged. v4 adds several explanatory sentences, an Impact Statement, correspondence and publication information, and removes the unresolved Appendix G reference with its accompanying sentence.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 3 to page 4, and Figure 3 moves from page 7 to page 8 alongside Figure 4. Figure 2's caption expands with model-size information. The four figure graphics and table structures are retained, with limited layout reflow.

improvement.justification: The added masking and baseline implementation details, parameter-count disclosures, and project/code pointer modestly improve reproducibility and comparison transparency. Removing the unresolved Appendix G reference cleans the text but also removes a useful sensitivity qualification. With the experiments and evidence unchanged, the net quality gain is limited.
